title: UUIDv4 vs. BIGINT / ULID for Primary Keys
realWorldScenario: A microservices application generates customer IDs on the client side before writing to PostgreSQL, but database writes slow down significantly after reaching 50 million rows.
questionStatement: Why does random UUIDv4 cause severe B-Tree index fragmentation and write degradation at scale? How do sequential identifiers (BIGINT, UUIDv7, ULID) solve this?
expectedConcepts: B-Tree page splits and cache thrashing
hints: Think about what happens to a sorted B-Tree when inserts arrive in totally random order.
